commits.messageBody:
RAG pipelines push a system prompt, the user question, retrieved documents
and chat history into an LLM node with no accounting of the model's context
window. When the total exceeds the limit the provider rejects the request or
silently truncates, and no node in the catalog trims content by token budget
before the LLM call.

context_optimizer is a questions -> questions filter that counts tokens with
tiktoken, allocates a per-component budget (system prompt / query / documents
/ history, configurable percentages), truncates on sentence boundaries, keeps
the highest-scoring documents that fit, and compacts the middle of the
conversation history. Requests that already fit pass through unchanged and no
extra model call is made.

Context-window sizes are resolved from the live model catalog first -- the
modelTotalTokens values on the preconfig profiles of the sibling llm_* nodes,
which tools/sync_models keeps in step with the providers -- so ids such as
gpt-5.4, claude-sonnet-4-6 and models/gemini-3.1-pro-preview resolve without
this node hard-coding them. MODEL_LIMITS remains as a fallback for
deployments without the llm_* nodes and for the abbreviated family aliases no
provider publishes; it was refreshed against that catalog. This answers the
open MODEL_LIMITS note from #527 without reaching for
IInvokeLLM.GetContextLength(), which is only available after beginFilter.

classType is "text" so the docs sidebar files the node under Text rather than
the unmapped "transform" fallback category (packages/docs/scripts/lib/
gather.js NODE_CATEGORIES). util-text.svg is co-located because the engine
resolves icons relative to services.json since 488d076b and otherwise logs
"Icon : **** MISSING" and renders the unknown glyph.

The unit suite guards that fallback: one test asserts MODEL_LIMITS and the
live catalog never state a different window for an id they both carry, so a
stale table entry fails loudly instead of changing the budget depending on
whether the llm_* nodes are deployed. The catalog discovery test asserts
structure -- non-empty mapping, positive integer windows, no discovered
provider silently dropped -- rather than naming model ids that tools/
sync_models is free to rename. The services.json test block carries a comment
noting that tiktoken downloads its BPE vocabulary on first use and that
TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR pre-seeds it.

Continues #527.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Every node PR merged since July adds a row to the docs/README-nodes.md
catalog and a line under CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] / Added; do the same for
context_optimizer.

The hand-maintained "121 node directories -> 151 services" sentence and the

stale on develop (137 directories / 183 services*.json today), so bumping
them by one would propagate a wrong number and add conflict surface with

commits.messageBody:
…r budget

Addresses the six CodeRabbit threads on the rebased head of #1489.

- IInstance.py:102 (Data Integrity, Major) -- FIXED. writeQuestions no longer
  collapses question.questions to its first entry. Every QuestionText is kept
  and rewritten in place; when the merged query is truncated the entries share
  the query allowance, each keeping a slice proportional to its own size via
  the new ContextOptimizer.truncate_each_to_budget. No other filter node on
  develop destroys the list (rerank_cohere/IInstance.py:55 and
  store_elasticsearch/IInstance.py:52 read questions[0] but forward it intact,
  guardrails/IInstance.py:58 joins every entry and forwards unchanged), while
  embedding_transformer/sentenceTransformer.py:135 writes an embedding per
  entry -- so the drop was losing real downstream data.

- optimizer.py:334 (Functional Correctness, Minor) -- FIXED. resolve_model_limit
  builds one candidate list (full id, then the bare name for a scoped id) and
  uses it for both the catalog and MODEL_LIMITS. With an empty catalog,
  'openai/gpt-5' resolved to DEFAULT_MODEL_LIMIT (128000) instead of 400000 and
  warned; it now resolves through the table, which is what the table is for.

- optimizer.py:357 (Stability, Minor) -- FIXED. _parse_pct rejects NaN, which
  satisfied neither range check and then raised
  "ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer" inside allocate_budget,
  failing the whole optimize() call. inf/-inf keep clamping as before.

- optimizer.py:541 (Functional Correctness, Minor) -- FIXED. truncate_to_budget
  re-measures the joined sentences before returning them. The per-sentence
  tally excludes the joining spaces, so the result could exceed max_tokens:
  measured, 'Alpha beta gamma. 12345 67890.' costs 11 cl100k tokens against a
  10-token budget.

- optimizer.py:588 (Functional Correctness, Minor) -- FIXED. summarize_history
  reserves the placeholder's widest wording (the omitted count is substituted
  only after the budget is fixed, and costs 5 more tokens than the bare
  marker), so the returned list stays inside max_tokens -- measured, 12
  messages against a 25-token budget returned 29. The adjacent single-message
  path had the same defect (it ignored the role overhead the docstring
  promises to reserve) and is fixed the same way.

- optimizer.py:762 (Refactor, Major) -- FIXED. optimize() derives the encoding
  from effective_model and threads it through every count, so a model override
  can no longer apply one model's limit with another model's tokenizer. The
  encoding is reported in metadata.

26 new tests; each fix was mutation-checked by reverting it and confirming the
matching test fails. Suite: 124 passed under real tiktoken 0.14.0 and under the
suite's whitespace stub. The three ci_tiny dynamic cases in services.json were
replayed and produce identical results, so no expectation changed.

commits.messageBody:
… overhead

`ContextOptimizer.summarize_history` promises never to exceed `max_tokens`,
but two branches could still overshoot. Every returned message costs
`count_tokens(role) + 4` before a single content token is spent, so when
`max_tokens` is below that floor even an empty-content message breaks the
contract: the `len(messages) == 1` branch and the `budget_for_recent <= 0`
fallback both computed a negative `content_budget`, got `''` back from
`truncate_to_budget`, and returned a ~5-token message anyway.

Guard both branches with `if content_budget < 0: return []` and state the
empty-list case in the docstring. A budget exactly equal to the overhead
still returns one empty-content message, which costs exactly the budget.

Adds `TestHistorySummarization::test_budget_below_role_overhead_returns_empty`,
covering both branches across every budget below the floor plus the boundary
at the floor itself. Mutation-checked by disabling the guard, which fails the
new test.

Reported by CodeRabbit as an outside-diff comment on 2026-07-08.

commits.messageBody:
resolve_model_limit() already falls back from a provider-scoped id to its
bare name, so 'openai/gpt-5' resolves the 400k gpt-5 context window.
encoding_name_for_model() did not strip that prefix: the
_MODEL_ENCODING_OVERRIDES lookup missed, tiktoken.encoding_for_model()
raised KeyError for the scoped name and the count silently fell back to
cl100k_base. The gpt-5 window was therefore measured with the gpt-4
tokenizer -- on Japanese text that overcounts by ~21% (510 vs 420 tokens
for the same string), so the node truncates content it did not need to.

encoding_name_for_model() now builds the same (full, bare) candidate
tuple resolve_model_limit() uses and tries the override table and then
tiktoken against each. Unscoped ids produce a one-element tuple and are
byte-for-byte unaffected.

Also validate model_name at the config boundary. Config.getNodeConfig()
merges profile defaults into the raw pipeline config without type
checking, so a hand-written "model_name": null reached rsplit() and
raised AttributeError inside beginGlobal, taking the node down before it
served a single record. Non-strings and blank strings now fall back to
the documented DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME with a warning, matching how
max_context_tokens and the budget percentages are already handled.

Adds TestScopedIdEncoding (15 cases) and TestModelNameValidation (17
cases); the suite goes 125 -> 157. Both were mutation-checked by
reverting each fix in isolation: 6 and 12 failures respectively.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
